newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-West Indies suffer middle-order collapse.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-West Indies suffer middle-order collapse.

text.p: Pakistan off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq took four wickets on Tuesday as West Indies collapsed to be 181 all out in their World Series limited overs match at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Saqlain, 20, and paceman Waqar Younis tore the heart out of the West Indies' middle and lower orders in the space of ten overs, West Indies losing their last eight wickets for 25 runs between the 37th and 47th overs.
Saqlain bamboozled the West Indies with a series of carefully flighted off-spinners, taking three wickets for 11 runs in the space of five overs and ending with four for 17 from nine overs.
Waqar, who returned after three weeks off with a shoulder injury, was back to his devastating best.
He took three for 35 from his 10 overs and showed he had not lost the ability to extract his trademark reverse swing as the ball became worn late in the innings.
West Indies had appeared to be cruising towards a total above 250, with slight left-hander Shivnarine Chanderpaul scoring at will on a gentle pitch.
But Chanderpaul fell for 72 with the score on 156 and a West Indies middle-order without star batsman Brian Lara, who was rested from this match, collapsed in swift fashion.
West Indies have won their last five World Series matches in a row, including three in the last nine days, relying on sparkling batting from Lara to chase down hefty totals.
The match is a dress rehearsal for the first of the best-of-three World Series finals in Sydney on Saturday.

West Indies and Pakistan are already assured of places in the finals, with host Australia eliminated from the tri-nation series when they lost to West Indies on Sunday. Australia last missed a place in the annual tri-nations series in the 1979/80 season.
West Indies went into the match with a depleted bowling attack, adding to Pakistan's hopes of victory as they chase a meagre total.
Tour captain Courtney Walsh and fellow fast bowler Curtly Ambrose were rested, with second-string pacemen Patterson Thompson and Nixon Mclean starting in their place.
